fact: The digital transition ministry inaugurated two modular public-administration datacenters in Ouagadougou on 23 January 2026, built to hold the state's civil registry, health, tax and civil service data and platforms; 3,000 TB storage, cost over 15bn FCFA.
The Prime Minister inaugurated two modular datacenters of the government cloud in Ouagadougou on 23 January 2026, to host, operate and secure all public data.

The government cloud portal run by ANPTIC (Ministry of Digital Transition) states that the G-Cloud infrastructure, with 4 datacenters and 8 cloud nodes, hosts 139 websites and 622 virtual machines and runs government applications (state messaging, gov.bf directory, Oracle business applications such as SIGASPE and E-conseil des ministres); the page is undated, so as_of is its 2026-08-05 capture date.

The ministry's communications office says the country inaugurated in January 2026 two modular datacentres of its government cloud, with nearly 3,000 TB of storage and capacity for over 7,000 virtual machines, to host citizen files, health and financial data and critical systems at home.
The ministry says it has made control of infrastructure, platforms and data a national priority under the 'Zero data abroad' first stage of its twelve digital transformation projects.
The ABDI executive director said two public-administration datacentres were recently commissioned in Burkina Faso.
The ABDI executive director cited a national datacentre project planned for a 2028 horizon.

The ministry's secretary general said the government's twelve digital projects include building national data centres, and that the 'zero data abroad' vision is the basis for sovereign governance of administration, business and citizen data.
The government plans the migration and repatriation of data to the new national datacenters in 2026, according to the ministry in charge of digital transition's CASEM session of 23 March 2026.
The article says the FasoSign keys, certificates and data stay hosted on national territory under the control of Burkinabe engineers.
Burkina Faso's AI roadmap 2026-2030 aims for national hosting of at least 80% of the data concerned and for its data and models to stay under state control and ownership, Dr Yaya Traore said.
